    EmailLinkIssuer
    WhoEmailLinkAutoConfiguration.emailLinkIssuer(EmailCredentialService emailCredentialService, WhoService whoService, EmailLinkTokenRepository emailLinkTokenRepository, org.springframework.beans.factory.ObjectProvider<WhoEmails> whoEmails, org.springframework.beans.factory.ObjectProvider<WhoEmailRenderer> renderers, EmailLinkSettings settings, Clock clock, WhoEventPublisher whoEventPublisher, org.springframework.beans.factory.ObjectProvider<io.micrometer.observation.ObservationRegistry> observationRegistry)
    Issues a sign-in link and code and sends them, only to the address of an active identity and not again within the resend interval.
    EmailLinkLoginMethod
    WhoEmailLinkAutoConfiguration.emailLinkLoginMethod(WhoOneTimeTokenService tokenService, JsonGenerateOneTimeTokenRequestResolver generateRequestResolver, EmailLinkGenerationSuccessHandler generationSuccessHandler, org.springframework.beans.factory.ObjectProvider<tools.jackson.databind.json.JsonMapper> jsonMapper, JsonAuthenticationHandlers handlers, WhoService whoService, EmailLinkTokenRepository emailLinkTokenRepository, EmailLinkSettings settings, Clock clock, WhoEventPublisher whoEventPublisher, WhoPaths paths)
    The provider and the converter are built here rather than published as beans: a lone AuthenticationProvider bean would become Spring Security's global one and switch off the application's UserDetailsService, and Spring's resource server takes any AuthenticationConverter bean as its own, so bearer requests would be read as sign-in codes.
    InvitationService
    WhoEmailLinkAutoConfiguration.invitationService(WhoService whoService, EmailCredentialService emailCredentialService, org.springframework.beans.factory.ObjectProvider<InvitationRoles> roles, EmailLinkIssuer emailLinkIssuer, org.springframework.context.ApplicationEventPublisher applicationEventPublisher, org.springframework.transaction.PlatformTransactionManager transactionManager, Clock clock)
    Invites people by email address: creates the identity, registers the address, assigns the roles and publishes IdentityInvited in one transaction, then sends the sign-in link.

    WhoSpringSecurityAutoConfiguration.whoSessionSecurityContextRepository(WhoService whoService, WhoSessions whoSessions, Clock clock, WhoEventPublisher whoEventPublisher, org.springframework.beans.factory.ObjectProvider<StatelessLoginMethod> statelessMethods)
